COMMENTS: Description: Isisuk Cliff in local terms is called Isisuk Cave. This cave is in the traditional ownership of Kuntui and Psakor. This site is a sleeping house for local residents when travelling across the border (return) from Kampung Kibay to the Papua New Guinea region and vice versa. In this bedroom there are barriers for men and women. The part for women is called the birthing house. This barrier is characterised by a small hole on the cliff that resembles the footprints of a human foot. The footprint of this foot is one metre above the ground. Based on the story of the people, this footprint is the footprint of their ancestors. However, as a result of the observation of the research team, the footprint is a natural formation. Isisuk Cliff until now is still used by the Kibay community as a place to live when travelling both to Papua New Guinea and vice versa. A lot of vandalism was found on this cliff with graffiti in the form of pictures and people's names. The handwriting uses Roman letters. In addition to paintings, fragments of animal bones and animal teeth were also found. Based on the identification of the shape of Tebing Isisuk wall painting, the shape of the image can be classified consisting of figurative and non-figurative images and there are images that have faded and are difficult to identify the shape.
